english.title: Carry on a regulated activity when not an authorised / exempt person
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), contravened a general prohibition by carrying on a regulated activity, namely **(..SPECIFY THE REGULATED ACTIVITY..), when not an authorised or exempt person
english.legislation: Contrary to section 23(1) of the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
carried on regulated activity
when not authorised / exempt

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) 'Regulated activity' is defined in section 22 of the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000.
(ii) Section 23(3) of the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 provides that in proceedings for an offence under this section it is a defence for the accused to show that he took all reasonable precautions and exercised all due diligence to avoid committing the offence.
(iii) Section 401 of the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 provides that proceedings for offences may be instituted in England and Wales only by the Authority or the Secretary of State or by or with the consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions.

other.penalty:
Summary: Six months imprisonment and of a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: Two years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
